title: CI: generate terraform-docs and enforce README consistency
author: Sahana Iyer
body: Motivation: We’ve been updating module READMEs manually and we’re already drifting between what variables/outputs actually exist vs what the docs claim. This gets especially painful for Private pilots because Solutions/PS are copying snippets and we end up debugging “missing var” issues that are really just stale READMEs. This PR adds terraform-docs generation and enforces that generated README sections stay in sync as part of CI. Scope: (1) Add terraform-docs config and a standard marker block pattern used by all modules. (2) Add a Makefile target and a pre-commit hook to generate docs locally. (3) Add GitHub Actions job that fails if README.md differs from generated output. (4) Update existing module READMEs to include the generated sections and normalize formatting (tables for inputs/outputs). Notes/Decisions: We only generate inside explicit markers to avoid rewriting human sections (overview, topology notes, security caveats). CI uses a pinned terraform-docs version to keep formatting deterministic. For now, we run doc generation only for modules/ (not examples/) to avoid noise; we can expand later. How to use: Run `make docs` before pushing; or install pre-commit and it will run terraform-docs on staged changes. CI will fail with a diff if you forget. Risk: Low; doc-only + CI enforcement. The only functional impact is that PRs touching variables/outputs must also update README markers (auto-generated).
commits: ci(terraform-docs): add pinned terraform-docs install + docs-check job
build(make): add `make docs` and `make docs-check` targets
pre-commit: add terraform-docs hook and repo-wide config
docs(modules): add BEGIN/END markers and regenerate READMEs for vpc-baseline, vpc-endpoints, security-groups-baseline
chore: align README headings and tables for consistent rendering
checks: CI summary: terraform fmt (pass), terraform validate (pass), tflint (skipped in this PR; introduced in PR-248), docs-check (pass), unit smoke (pass). docs-check details: runs terraform-docs v0.17.0 in docker/pinned binary, executes `make docs`, then asserts `git diff --exit-code` is clean.
conversation: Elliot Price (review): Can we keep the human-written module overview at the top? The generated sections are fine but I don’t want terraform-docs to rewrite the security caveats we’ve added for Private. Also, please add a short note to CONTRIBUTING so external contributors don’t get surprised by a failing CI check. Sahana Iyer (author): Yep — generation is constrained to markers only; human sections stay intact. Added CONTRIBUTING note and an explicit “Generated docs block” explanation. Irene Choi (review): Good. One request: pin the terraform-docs version in CI to avoid formatting churn. Also can you make the failure message actionable (tell folks to run make docs)? Sahana Iyer (author): Done. Pinned to v0.17.0 and updated the workflow step to echo instructions when diff is detected. Bruno Silva (review): Love this. For PS workflows: can we also mention `make docs` in the module README itself? Some folks won’t read CONTRIBUTING. Sahana Iyer (author): Added a short line in CONTRIBUTING only for now to avoid repeating in every README; happy to add later if we see confusion. Elliot Price (review): Approved once pinned version is in. Irene Choi (review): Approved. Bruno Silva (review): Approved.
release_notes: Internal: Module README inputs/outputs are now generated via terraform-docs. CI will fail if README markers are out of date; run `make docs` (or pre-commit) to update before pushing.
